newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shares close weaker in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shares close weaker in thin trade.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange slipped in weak trading as foreign investors stayed away from the market and local investors were unnerved by exchange rate volatility, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index fell 0.37 percent to 9,182.90, as 21 stocks fell, 12 rose and 10 closed flat.
With foreign interest focused on other Latin American markets, trading levels were low with just 877 trades worth 4.542 billion bolivars ($9.2 million).
Econoinvest broker Gabriel Osio said that "there is some uncertainty over the exchange rate."
The Venezuelan bolivar, which depreciated just 2.5 percent in the first half of the year, has weakened by another 0.5 percent in the last three days.
"The (Central Bank) is letting the bolivar slide a little more than people expected...buyers are waiting to see what will happen," Osio said.
Brokers added that the market had very firm support and looked set to remain broadly stable for the next few sessions.

Among leading stocks, bellwether Electricidad de Caracas fell 8.00 bolivars to 798.00 bolivars, telephone company CANTV fell 24.00 bolivars to 3,001.00 bolivars while cement company Vencemos class 1 stock fell 4.00 bolivars to 1045.00 bolivars and class 2 stock fell 7.00 bolivars to 933.00 bolivars.
